newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia PM says he expects to stay as leader.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia PM says he expects to stay as leader.

text.p: Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek, whose Liberal Democrats won most votes in a general election on November 10, said on Monday he expected to be called by President Milan Kucan to form the next government.
"The Liberal Democrats won and have the right to the prime minister's post. Anything else would be an election hoax," Drnovsek told a news conference.

The Liberal Democrats, who won 25 of the 90 parliamentary seats, face an alliance of three rightwing parties, known as the "Slovenian Spring", which just missed scoring an absolute majority in parliament by just one seat.
The alliance, comprising the rightist People's Party, centre-right Social Democrats and Christian Democrats, took 45 seats and hoped to form the core of Slovenia's next administration.
People's Party leader Marjan Podobnik said last week that the alliance could not work with the Liberal Democrats unless Drnovsek stepped down as premier.
Drnovsek made clear his Liberal Democrats would play a part in the new government only if he remained as prime minister.

"The next four years will be crucial for Slovenia," Drnovsek said. "An unstable government would not be able to end the processes that are most important for our country, such as joining the European Union and NATO and entering the club of developed countries (OECD)."
Slovenia, which broke away from the Yugoslavia in 1991, hopes to join the EU by the year 2001 and to become a full member of NATO in 1999.
"The elections resulted in an undecided outcome and it is hard to say when the new government will be formed," Drnovsek said.
He said he would talk to the leaders of all the other parliamentary parties to find partners for a new coalition.

Kucan is likely to start calling political leaders for consultations this week before the parties begin what is expected to be a lengthy series of discussions to settle the shape of the new government.
